page.layout: Two coin medallions centred at the top, with engraved legends; below them one column of text in two paragraphs. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: LYSIMACHVS illustri quidem Macedoniæ loco natus, sed virtutis ornamentis omni nobilitate clarior extitit.hic animi magnitudine, Philosophia, virium gloria, omnes per quos Oriens domitus est,vicit. A Callisthene,quamuis truncato auribus, naribus, ac labiis, præcepta Philosophiæ accipere non erubuit.hunc ferocissimo leoni obiecit Alexander:leonis linguam hic statim avulsit: chariorem inde habuit eum Alexander,quem imprudens cùm in fronte vulnerasset, diadema sibi demptum Rex alligandi vulneris causa, capiti eius imposuit, quod auspicium primum regalis maiestatis Lysimacho fuit. Regnavit itaque in Macedonia anno mundi 3676. ante Christum natum 286. Post mortem Alexandri cùm inter successores provinciæ dividerentur, Thraces,& Pontici, ferocissimæ gentes, illi quasi omnium fortissimo assignatę sunt. De cuius morte ac filiorum eius 15. vide Justin.lib.17. Lysimachiam condidit, quæ terræ motu corruit.

ANTIGONVS Gonatas , Demetrij Asiæ regis filius, apud Macedones regnat anno mundi 3686. ante Christum natum 276. Pyrrhus Antigonum fugat: Macedoniam occupat:post cuius mortem Peloponnesij Antigono traduntur: tandem multiplici bello pressus, in speciem castrorum parua manu adversus cæteros relicta, totis viribus in Gallos contendit, quos vicit. Interim Alexander Rex Epiri in ultionem mortis Pyrrhi patris sui, Macedoniam depopulatur, & capit: Demetrius Antigoni filius eam recipit, regnóque Epiri Alexandrum spoliat. Cosulito Justi. lib.25.& 26. ac Plutar.in Pau.Aemi.

page.notes: The two medallions are illustrations, not running text. Left coin: a laureate head in profile facing right, with the legend LYSIMACHVS around the rim. Right coin: a helmeted head in profile facing right, with the legend ANTIGONVS partly visible, reading TI / GO / NAS and a partly legible word on the lower left. Its outer legend is not fully readable, so it is not transcribed. Ampersands are written as & in the XML. The printed text in the paragraph beginning "Thraces" is set as "Thraces,& Pontici". The word "Cosulito" is printed that way and is kept as printed.
